assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theoretical prediction (flat bands at a magic twist angle, from a continuum band-structure model) followed by experimental realisation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable, clean platform. It opened twistronics and moire materials as a new way to engineer correlated electron states, with a very large follow-on literature. Conceptually clear and original, and a rare case where an electronic-structure prediction led directly to a new experimental field.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald calculation (2011) is the theoretical origin and Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the decisive 2018 experiments. The three-person configuration pairs prediction with experiment cleanly. Other groups made important early or parallel contributions (for example in earlier twisted-bilayer theory and in related experiments), so the boundary of credit is arguable but a three-person prize is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Observations of correlated insulators and superconductivity have been reproduced by many independent groups since 2018, and the band-structure picture is well established. The nature of the superconducting pairing is still debated, but the discovery itself is solid and the field is mature enough for recognition.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconducting state remains unresolved.
Contributions of other experimental groups to the early observations may complicate the experimental credit.
I rely on my own knowledge of the early twisted-graphene theory literature and have not independently checked priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Z2 topological classification of time-reversal-invariant insulators, the quantum spin Hall state, and its realisation in HgTe quantum wells are a conceptually deep and original development. The field has become central to modern condensed matter physics and linked spin-orbit coupling in band structures to protected edge and surface states, an area where first-principles materials calculations have played a major part.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the foundational theoretical step (2005), and Molenkamp's group made the decisive experimental QSH observation (2007), following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Hasan's three-dimensional topological insulator work is also major, but a three-person limit forces a choice. Zhang's death and the theoretical credit for the HgTe proposal and the three-dimensional theory (Moore, Balents, Fu) lie outside the supplied names, so the allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. Many independent confirmations by transport and photoemission, and a stable interpretation. The 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions and topological phases in 1D and quantum Hall systems, but the Z2 insulators are a distinct discovery and recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize could weigh against the candidate for some members.
Hasan's 3D topological insulator experiments are omitted from my proposed trio, which may be judged unfair.
The theoretical credit for the HgTe quantum well proposal lies partly outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is exact in infinite dimensions and gave the first controlled, non-perturbative description of the Mott transition and strongly correlated metals. Combined with density functional theory (DFT+DMFT) it became a standard tool for realistic correlated materials, including transition-metal oxides, f-electron systems and actinides. Its impact on how correlated materials are understood and calculated is broad and lasting. It is a theoretical method rather than a single discovery, which is a consideration for Nobel practice.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit, Georges and Kotliar established the mapping to a self-consistent quantum impurity problem, and Muller-Hartmann also contributed (he is not among the credited names and I understand he is deceased). Vollhardt, Georges and Kotliar is a reasonable trio but omits Metzner. The allocation between the formal limit and the impurity mapping is somewhat ambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Established for over three decades, with extensive validation against experiments (spectroscopy, optical conductivity, phase diagrams). Cluster extensions and ab initio combinations continue to develop, but the central framework is stable.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee treats a theoretical method as a discovery in the sense of the Nobel statutes.
Credit omitting Metzner, and the Muller-Hartmann contribution, is a real allocation problem.
As a practitioner of related methods I may overweight the method's importance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and the later coherent-tunnelling enhancement in MgO barriers, underpin modern hard-disk read heads and non-volatile magnetic memory. It combines spin-dependent tunnelling physics, which is well understood from electronic-structure arguments about symmetry-selective tunnelling, with major technological impact. It is a natural successor to the 2007 giant magnetoresistance prize.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported room-temperature TMR in 1995, and Yuasa (and Parkin, who is not among the credited names) reported giant TMR in MgO junctions in 2004. The supplied trio covers the key experimental steps, but the omission of Parkin and the early work of Julliere in 1975 complicates the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and commercially deployed for many years. Theory and experiment agree on the coherent-tunnelling mechanism.
uncertainties: Omission of Parkin from the credited names makes the MgO-era allocation incomplete.
The Committee may regard it as largely covered by the 2007 GMR prize.
Priority of Julliere's 1975 observation is not addressed in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism identifies a third fundamental class of collinear magnetic order, with zero net magnetisation but spin-split bands from crystal symmetry rather than relativistic spin-orbit coupling. This is a clean symmetry-based concept with direct implications for spintronics, and many materials candidates have been identified by first-principles calculations. It is conceptually significant and original.
assessment.attribution: Šmejkal, Jungwirth and Sinova developed the symmetry classification and the unified theoretical picture around 2019-2022, with related earlier contributions from other groups (including Japanese and other theory groups on non-relativistic spin splitting). Experimental confirmations in MnTe and CrSb came from several groups. The theory trio is a plausible configuration, but the experimental credit is distributed and unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Early. Direct spectroscopic evidence appeared only in 2023-2024 and the field is expanding quickly. The core symmetry argument is solid, but the number of confirmed materials and device demonstrations is still small, so recognition now would be premature rather than overdue.
uncertainties: Maturity is the main concern, since independent confirmation is recent and limited.
Credit for earlier work on non-relativistic spin splitting by other groups is unresolved.
The extent to which the real-world device impact will follow is unknown.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics realised strong light-matter coupling with superconducting circuits and gave the architecture (dispersive readout, microwave resonators) that underlies most superconducting quantum processors. It is original, clearly defined, and has broad impact on quantum technology and on quantum optics in a solid-state setting.
assessment.attribution: Blais proposed the cQED architecture (2004), Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling (2004). This three-person configuration maps well to theory plus the two experimental groups. Other contributors, such as the Yale group's transmon development (Koch, Schoelkopf and others) and the Saclay work, are outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with many independent implementations and a stable interpretation. Timing is complicated by the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits, which recognised neighbouring work and may make an immediate follow-up less likely.
uncertainties: The closeness to the 2025 prize may reduce the room for a second superconducting-circuit award soon.
Credit for the transmon and other circuit developments is outside the supplied names.
This is outside my own research area, so my comparative judgement is less secure.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetic skyrmions are topologically protected spin textures observed in chiral magnets and in thin films. The discovery combined theory based on Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction with direct observation, and links topology to magnetism with potential for low-energy spintronics. It is a clear and important discovery in magnetism, with a rich interplay with atomistic spin dynamics and first-principles calculations of the interactions.
assessment.attribution: Pfleiderer's group found the skyrmion lattice in MnSi (2009), Tokura's group provided real-space imaging in 2010, and Wiesendanger's group demonstrated an atomic-scale skyrmion lattice and writing and deleting of individual skyrmions. The theoretical foundation by Bogdanov and others, and the contributions of Rossler, are not among the credited names, which leaves a gap.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed, with room-temperature skyrmions in multilayers also reported. Applications such as racetrack memory remain unproven, so technological recognition is not yet established, though the basic physics is solid.
uncertainties: The theoretical origin in the work of Bogdanov and colleagues is outside the supplied names.
Device relevance remains largely prospective.
Priority among several experimental groups is disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Neodymium-iron-boron magnets are the strongest commercial permanent magnets and are central to electric motors, wind turbines, and data storage. The discovery combined intrinsic magnetic properties (large saturation magnetisation and uniaxial anisotropy from the 4f-3d interplay) with metallurgical processing. Societal and technological impact is enormous, though the work is materials discovery with less new fundamental concept than other candidates.
assessment.attribution: Sagawa (sintered route, Sumitomo Special Metals) and Croat (melt-spun route, General Motors) announced the compound independently in 1983-1984, so a two-person prize is natural and fair. Other contributors to the crystal structure determination are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of industrial use and well understood microscopic origin. Timing is unproblematic scientifically, but the Committee's preference for discovery over materials engineering counts against it.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee considers it fundamental physics rather than materials engineering.
As a magnetism theorist I may be inclined to favour it more than others would.
